**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 6, §6.1. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

A delivery's actual fulfilment time can be uncertain even when distance and item count are known. Probability begins by stating the universe of possible outcomes and which events we wish to measure.

## Formal relationship

$$
(\Omega,\mathcal F,P),\quad P(\Omega)=1,\quad P(A)\geq0
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Imagine one randomly selected order from our six-record teaching dataset. Let Omega be its six row IDs, each equally likely. The event A='time at least 16 minutes' contains three IDs, so P(A)=3/6=0.5. That empirical experiment is not a claim about all future orders.

## Interpretation and limitations

A sigma-algebra specifies measurable events; a probability measure assigns them consistently. When outcomes are real-valued times, the model typically uses a continuous sample space instead of six equally likely records.

## Explain it yourself

Define an event B for orders with more than one item. Compute its empirical probability from the dataset.
